item.text:
**6B.6 Research Note**

Overall: **mostly yes, with clear limits**. Kishida’s 2024 record shows real crisis mitigation for the Noto earthquake, plus humanitarian support for Ukraine and civilian-protection diplomacy around Gaza. The main limit is that economic suffering was still severe: the government itself acknowledged weak consumer demand, falling real wages, and weak-yen pressure on households, so relief was meaningful but incomplete.

**Positive**
- **Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 5, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/05kaiken.html | Kishida ordered rescue operations, road reopenings, helicopter transport for isolated communities, and a package to support victims’ daily lives and livelihoods, which is direct evidence of reducing avoidable disaster suffering. | QIDs: `6B.6`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`
- **Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 11, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/11kaiken.html | He urged secondary evacuation for vulnerable evacuees to reduce cold-weather hardship, disease risk, and shelter overcrowding, showing concrete harm-reduction in a live disaster. | QIDs: `6B.6`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`
- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida on His Visit to Ishikawa Prefecture to Confirm the Situation of the Area Affected by the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 1, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html | Kishida said the government had used more than 550 billion yen in reserve funds across five tranches to restore infrastructure, lifelines, housing, and livelihoods, while admitting some recovery tasks still lagged. | QIDs: `6B.6`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`
- **Japan-Ukraine Summit Meeting (Summary)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 13, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/13ukraine.html | Japan signed an accord covering humanitarian support, recovery and reconstruction, electricity assistance, and mine action, which is direct evidence of reducing conflict-displacement suffering. | QIDs: `6B.6`
- **Speech by Prime Minister Kishida at the Opening Plenary Session of the Summit on Peace in Ukraine** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 15, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/15speech.html | Kishida framed Japan’s support as assistance for electricity and mine clearance so Ukrainians could safely rebuild daily life, tying aid to civilian protection and recovery. | QIDs: `6B.6`
- **Adoption of the United Nations Security Council resolution 2735 on the Situation in Gaza** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | June 11, 2024 | https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00366.html | Japan backed a ceasefire/hostage-release resolution and urged compliance with international humanitarian law to prevent further civilian casualties. | QIDs: `6B.6`

**Negative / Mixed**
- **Japan downgrades view of economy on sluggish consumer spending** | Reuters | February 21, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japan-downgrades-view-of-economy-on-sluggish-consumer-spending-3309375 | The government downgraded its economic view because consumer spending was stalling, real wages had fallen for 21 straight months, and the recovery remained bumpy, so avoidable suffering from the economic shock clearly persisted. | QIDs: `6B.6`, `5B.10`, `6B.5`
- **Japan warns of weak yen impact on households in government white paper** | Reuters | August 1, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-warns-of-weak-yen-impact-on-households-in-government-white-paper-3551065 | The government warned that the weak yen was hurting household sentiment and eroding purchasing power, which shows the 2024 response did not fully offset cost-of-living pain. | QIDs: `6B.6`, `5B.10`, `6B.5`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on **disasters**, **Ukraine-related displacement**, **Gaza civilian-protection diplomacy**, and **inflation/household shock**.
- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence on **pandemic-specific crisis relief** or **famine response**, which is unsurprising for Japan in 2024.
- Direct, independent service-delivery outcome metrics were sparse; most evidence comes from official statements plus Reuters reporting, so the conclusion is solid but not granular.
